Hyperliquid Strategies Expands Share Buyback Program to 100 Million USD Hyperliquid Strategies Inc. (NASDAQ: PURR), a HYPE-focused digital asset treasury company, has increased its share repurchase authorization from 30 million USD to 100 million USD, with approximately 72 million USD remaining available. The company also extended the program's expiration date from December 5, 2026, to October 31, 2027. Actual repurchases will depend on market conditions and management's discretion. — link

Highlight Clip: CME Chairman: Hyperliquid Will Struggle to Enter the U.S. Market Without Addressing KYC Requirements CME Chairman: Hyperliquid Will Struggle to Enter the U.S. Market Without Addressing KYC Requirements On October 20, 2026, CME Group CEO Terry Duffy said on Bloomberg's Odd Lots podcast that Hyperliquid cannot shift all regulatory responsibility to users or deployers by claiming it merely provides the underlying infrastructure. He argued that the lack of know-your-customer checks, combined with high leverage and automatic liquidation mechanisms, could trigger cascading liquidations and disrupt markets. Platforms have a duty to oversee trading and ensure fair and orderly market participation. He stressed that Hyperliquid must comply with U.S. law if it wants to enter the U.S. market, adding that, in his view, the operating model proposed by its founder Jeff Yan raises multiple compliance issues. — link

Argentine Judge Drops LIBRA Criminal Probe Against President Milei and Hayden Davis According to Reuters, Argentine federal judge Marcelo Martínez de Giorgi has dropped the criminal investigation into President Javier Milei, his sister Karina Milei, and U.S. businessman Hayden Davis over the LIBRA meme coin scandal, finding insufficient evidence of fraud. The judge ruled that while Milei’s endorsement on X may have amplified the token’s launch, it did not in itself constitute a fraudulent scheme. Milei promoted LIBRA in February 2025 before deleting his post as the token’s price collapsed. Blockchain researchers previously reported that eight wallets linked to the token’s creator withdrew approximately $99 million in cryptocurrency from the token’s trading market. — link

HTX Adds Russia to List of Restricted Jurisdictions, Following Bitget and MEXC According to Russian business media outlet RBC, cryptocurrency exchange HTX has included Russia in its list of restricted jurisdictions under its user agreement. The restrictions apply to individuals residing in or located in Russia, as well as companies registered or primarily operating there. Under the agreement, HTX may restrict access to its services, suspend withdrawals, or close affected accounts. Earlier in October, Bitget and MEXC also announced plans to discontinue services for Russian users. RBC did not specify when HTX's restrictions took effect. — link
